waterTemp.high.title: Nutrient water is too warm
waterTemp.high.why: Warm water holds less oxygen, so roots can suffocate and root rot can start.
steps: Shade or cover the reservoir and keep it out of direct sun.
Add sealed bottles of frozen water, or use a water chiller.
Make sure the air pump is running to add oxygen.

waterTemp.low.title: Nutrient water is too cold
waterTemp.low.why: Cold water slows root growth and nutrient uptake.
steps: Insulate the reservoir with foam sheets or a cover.
Use an aquarium heater set to about 20 °C.
Keep the reservoir off cold floors.

ph.high.title: pH is too high
ph.high.why: Above the target, plants cannot absorb iron and other nutrients, and new leaves turn yellow.
steps: Add pH Down (phosphoric acid) a few ml at a time.
Run the pump or stir for 15 minutes.
Test again and repeat until pH is back in range.

ph.low.title: pH is too low
ph.low.why: Acidic water can burn roots and lock out calcium and magnesium.
steps: Add pH Up (potassium hydroxide) a few ml at a time.
Run the pump or stir for 15 minutes.
Test again and repeat until pH is back in range.

ec.low.title: Nutrients are too weak
ec.low.why: Plants are using up the fertiliser. Growth slows and leaves turn pale.
steps: Add hydroponic nutrient A and B in equal amounts, following the label dose.
Mix well and check EC again after 15 minutes.
Check pH again after adding nutrients.

ec.high.title: Nutrients are too strong
ec.high.why: Too much fertiliser burns roots. Leaf tips turn brown and plants wilt.
steps: Top up the reservoir with clean water to dilute it.
If EC is still high, replace part of the solution.
Check that nutrients were not added twice.

dissolvedOxygen.low.title: Roots are short of oxygen
dissolvedOxygen.low.why: Without enough oxygen, roots turn brown and rot within hours to days.
steps: Check that the air pump is switched on and running.
Clean or replace blocked air stones and check the air tubes.
Cool the water if it is warm.

waterLevel.low.title: Reservoir is running low
waterLevel.low.why: If the pump runs dry, plants lose water and the pump can be damaged.
steps: Top up the reservoir with clean water.
Check pipes, channels and joints for leaks.
After topping up, check pH and EC again.

airTemp.high.title: Greenhouse is too hot
airTemp.high.why: Heat stress causes wilting, flower drop and bitter leafy greens.
steps: Open vents and side curtains, or run the fans.
Pull a shade net (about 50%) over the roof.
Use misting during the hottest hours (11 AM to 3 PM).

airTemp.low.title: Greenhouse is too cold
airTemp.low.why: Cold slows growth and can damage tender crops.
steps: Close vents and curtains in the evening.
Seal gaps in the plastic covering.
Water the floor in the morning, not at night.

humidity.high.title: Humidity is too high
humidity.high.why: Damp air encourages fungal diseases such as grey mould and mildew.
steps: Increase ventilation: open vents or run fans.
Avoid wetting the leaves when watering.
Remove dead leaves and keep space between plants.

humidity.low.title: Air is too dry
humidity.low.why: Plants lose water quickly and leaf edges can burn.
steps: Mist the floor and paths.
Use a shade net to reduce the sun.
Make sure the crop has enough water.

light.low.title: Not enough light
light.low.why: Low light makes plants stretch and slows growth.
steps: Clean dust and algae off the greenhouse roof.
Remove extra shade nets in cloudy weather.
Consider LED grow lights for cloudy seasons.

light.high.title: Light is too strong
light.high.why: Very strong sun can scorch leaves and overheat the greenhouse.
steps: Pull a shade net over the crop at midday.
Increase ventilation to remove heat.

co2.high.title: CO₂ is building up
co2.high.why: Stale air means poor ventilation. Very high CO₂ is also unsafe for workers.
steps: Open vents or run exhaust fans.
Make sure fuel heaters or generators vent outside.

co2.low.title: CO₂ is too low
co2.low.why: Plants need CO₂ to grow. It drops when the greenhouse stays closed all day.
steps: Open vents to bring in fresh air.
Ventilate more in the morning, when plants are most active.

substrateMoisture.low.title: Grow bags are drying out
substrateMoisture.low.why: Dry roots stop taking up water and nutrients, and plants wilt.
steps: Run an irrigation cycle now.
Check drippers for blockages.
Water more often in hot weather.

substrateMoisture.high.title: Grow bags are waterlogged
substrateMoisture.high.why: Too much water pushes air out of the roots and causes root rot.
steps: Pause irrigation until the medium dries a little.
Check that drainage holes are not blocked.
Shorten the irrigation time.
